title: I’m a trader who built a real-time SEC insider trading API with AI as my pair-programmer. Here’s what worked.
author: mathewarena
selftext:
I've been trading for years and wanted cleaner access to SEC insider trading filings (Forms 3, 4, 5). The data is public but the XML format is brutal. So I spent two weeks of evenings building a clean JSON API for it — with AI as my pair-programmer. Here's how that went and what I built.

It's a clean JSON API + real-time webhooks for every Form 3/4/5 filing. Polls SEC every 30 seconds, parses the XML, structures it, and you can either query it directly or get pinged when filings match your filters (ticker, transaction code, dollar amount).

There's a public live feed at edgarkit.com/live where you can watch insider trades hit SEC in real time — no signup needed. Also a "Try it now" widget on the docs page if you want to poke at the API without an API key.

Tech stack:  
\- Node.js + Express backend  
\- PostgreSQL (Render managed)  
\- Two background workers: one for ingestion, one for webhook dispatch  
\- Stripe for billing  
\- Static landing on Render

The AI workflow that actually worked: I described what I wanted at the architecture level, AI drafted the code, I tested it against real SEC data and debugged what broke. Gotchas I had to actually hunt down (these prove the product is real, not just a generated demo):

\- SEC's atom feed CIK= param accepts any-length CIK, not just zero-padded 10-digit (their docs lie)  
\- Daily index .idx files give dates as YYYYMMDD with no dashes, which silently breaks new Date()  
\- Some Form 4 fields are footnote-only dates that look like "footnote 1" instead of ISO strings  
\- fast-xml-parser entity expansion bombs on large filings unless you crank maxTotalExpansions to 1M  
\- One of the worst bugs: the 2-year historical backfill blocked realtime ingestion for 14 hours during a redeploy before I caught it

Pricing:  
\- Free: 1,000 calls/mo  
\- $19/mo: 25k/mo + 1 webhook  
\- $79/mo: 250k/mo + 10 webhooks

Current scale: \~280k filings indexed (2 years of history + live), polling every 30s, end-to-end webhook latency 30-60 sec from SEC.

Things I learned that I didn't expect:  
\- Stripe flagged me as a "regulated industry" — had to write a careful response explaining I'm a SaaS API, not a broker. Still in review.  
\- The /live page (auto-updating list of insider trades) is way more compelling than any "demo video" I could've made  
\- Building the API was the easy part. Writing the docs and pricing page took as long as the backend.

Genuinely curious what other folks here are building with AI on trading-adjacent projects. And if you've tried launching a trading dev tool, I'd love to compare notes.

Site: edgarkit.com
